issues.legal_issue: The special revisional authority may revise a verified claim that became final under the earlier claims regime, including a claim finalized on revision.
material_facts: A claim had been verified and valued under the earlier claims regime.
The Claims Commissioner had increased the valuation on revision, making the claim final under that regime.
The Settlement Commissioner, exercising the special revisional authority, initiated revision on his own motion.
issues.conclusion: The special revisional power extends to verified claims that became final under the earlier regime, including claims finalized by an order on revision.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(1)(b) of the Displaced Persons (Claims) Supplementary Act, 1954 authorizes the Chief Settlement Commissioner, subject to applicable rules, to revise any verified claim and make such order as he thinks fit. Section 2(f) defines a verified claim by reference to a claim for which a final order has been passed under the principal Act. The provision's unambiguous language is not restricted by the preamble, and the statutory scheme does not exclude claims finalized on revision.

predicates.special_revision_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the exercise of a special power to revise a verified claim.
predicates.claim_finalized_under_prior_scheme: A claim was finally determined under an earlier claims regime, including through a revisional order.
predicates.officer_initiated_revision: The revisional officer initiated the revision on the officer's own motion.

issues.definition: When a special revision concerns a claim finalized under an earlier claims regime and the officer initiates revision, the final claim is subject to revision on the officer's own motion.

issues.legal_issue: The special power to revise a verified claim extends to the valuation of the claim as well as verification of title.
material_facts: The claim concerned ownership of immovable property left behind by a displaced person.
The original decision and the order on revision both addressed the amount at which the claim was valued.
The special revisional authority sought to alter that valuation.
issues.conclusion: The special revisional power covers valuation as well as verification of title.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(f) of the Displaced Persons (Claims) Supplementary Act, 1954 defines a verified claim by reference to the final order under the principal Act. Under the principal Act, the Claims Officer determines both title and value, so the final order embraces both. Section 5(1)(b) therefore permits revision of valuation as part of revision of a verified claim.

predicates.special_revision_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the exercise of a special power to revise a verified claim.
predicates.final_claim_order_includes_valuation: The final determination of the claim addressed both the claimant's asserted interest and the value of the property.
predicates.valuation_revision_sought: The revisional officer sought to alter the value assigned to the claim.

issues.definition: When a special revision concerns a claim whose final determination included valuation and a change to that valuation is sought, the valuation is within the scope of revision.

issues.legal_issue: The residual ground in the special-revision rules is not restricted by ejusdem generis where the specified grounds do not form a common class, and it may cover grounds analogous to a specified valuation irregularity.
material_facts: The special-revision rules listed discovery of new evidence, correction of an apparent clerical or arithmetical mistake, gross or material irregularity or disparity in valuation, and any other sufficient reason as grounds for revision.
The first three listed grounds did not form a common class.
The grounds relied on by the revisional officer were regarded as analogous to the specified ground concerning irregularity or disparity in valuation.
issues.conclusion: The ejusdem generis rule did not restrict the residual ground; in any event, the grounds relied on were analogous to the specified valuation ground.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 18 of the Displaced Persons (Verification of Claims) Supplementary Rules, 1954 governs special revision and includes 'any other sufficient reason' as a ground. Ejusdem generis is an interpretive aid that applies when specified terms form an unexhausted class followed by general terms, and no intention to give the general words broader scope appears. The Court relied on M.M.B. Catholicos v. Mar Poulose when considering the appellant's comparison with Order 47 rule 1(c) of the Code of Civil Procedure, but held that rule 18's valuation ground differed from the grounds in that provision and that the first three grounds in rule 18 did not form a genus.

predicates.special_revision_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the exercise of a special power to revise a verified claim.
predicates.listed_grounds_do_not_form_common_class: The specifically listed grounds for revision do not share a common class or genus.
predicates.revision_ground_analogous_to_valuation_i: The ground relied on for revision is analogous to a specified ground concerning irregularity or disparity in valuation.

issues.definition: In a special revision, the residual ground can cover the basis for revision if the listed grounds do not form a common class or the basis is analogous to a specified valuation irregularity.

issues.legal_issue: An administrative revision order based on conjecture and surmise without legal evidence contains an error of law apparent on the record and may be quashed in writ proceedings.
material_facts: The revisional officer based conclusions at multiple points on conjecture and surmise without supporting legal evidence.
The officer disregarded important evidence and treated documents as forged without evidence supporting that finding.
A single judge quashed the revisional order in writ proceedings, but an appellate bench reversed that decision.
The Supreme Court agreed with the single judge and directed that the matter return to the revisional authority for a fresh decision in accordance with law.
issues.conclusion: The revisional order contained errors of law apparent on the record and was properly quashed; the matter was remitted for a fresh decision in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that findings based on conjecture and surmise without legal evidence, including an unsupported finding that documents were forged, disclose errors of law apparent on the record that may be challenged in proceedings under Article 226 of the Constitution. The Court restored the single judge's order and remitted the matter without expressing an opinion on the evidentiary value of the material concerning valuation.

predicates.appeal_from_reversal_of_writ_relief: The proceeding is an appeal from a decision reversing writ relief against an administrative order.
predicates.administrative_order_based_on_conjecture: The administrative decision-maker based material conclusions on conjecture or surmise without legal evidence supporting them.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the reversal of writ relief and the administrative order rests on conjecture without legal evidence, the order is quashed and the matter is remitted.
